status_rationale: Theorem-generation revision aligned with OrB32-v7 in namespace Spec2Lean.PTX.OrB32 and fixes prior strength issues: (1) a malformed hypothesis in the predicate-frame sketch is corrected to i.b, and (2) traceability IDs reference only existing semantic claims. No proofs are included.

unit.bounded_unit: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded unit `or.b32 d, a, b;` with optional predication
unit.scope_boundary: Only .b32 with optional predication is formalized. Destination/source2 are local bounded model types; source1 is register-only by architecture restriction; no malformed/exception behavior is added.

compliance_notes: No proofs are included in this stage.
No vacuous determinism claims; relational determinism is expressed over OrB32Step and not over arbitrary function extensionality.
No semantics are imported from unrelated units.

validation_obligations.title: Bounded instruction shape and ordering
validation_obligations.description: OrB32Instruction has fields (guard, d, a, b) with source1 register-only and source2 register-or-immediate, matching bounded-or syntax and architecture restriction.

validation_obligations.title: 32-bit bounded value and minimal state representation
validation_obligations.description: B32 is Fin (2^32); MachineState contains exactly valueRegs and predRegs with partial lookup via Option.

validation_obligations.title: No bypass constructs added
validation_obligations.description: Lean declarations under Spec2Lean.PTX.OrB32 contain no sorry, admit, axioms, or unsafe blocks.

theorem_obligations.intent: For fixed state and instruction, OrB32Step determines at most one post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If OrB32Step s i s1 and OrB32Step s i s2, then s1 = s2.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : OrB32Step s i s1) (h2 : OrB32Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
strength_risks: Constructor-mismatch case requires care: noExecuted and executed constructors are disjoint by evalGuard being some false vs some true.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation has both constructors (notExecuted and executed) in realistic states, so this is a substantive uniqueness property of the operational relation, not a definitional tautology.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on h1 and h2; if constructors differ derive contradiction on evalGuard equation; otherwise reduce to equality of updateDestination or reflexive equality.

theorem_obligations.intent: Show execOrB32 and OrB32Step agree: executed and notExecuted outcomes produce the same post-state relation and missing inputs correspond to no-step behavior.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) executed outcome implies step, (b) notExecuted outcome implies step, (c) any OrB32Step is realized by an execOrB32 outcome (some branch), (d) execOrB32 = none iff no OrB32Step holds.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_execOrB32_executed_iff_step (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) : execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ↔ OrB32Step s i s'
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Equivalence between executed outcomes and executed steps, with separate supporting lemmas for notExecuted and none/none-step completeness.
strength_risks: Must not accidentally strengthen behavior: none/partiality is intentional for missing predicate or source operands per OQ-OR-2 / PTX-OR-SEM1-008.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Neither function nor relation is total in this bounded model; both some and none cases occur, so partial-equivalence statements are substantive.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold both definitions; split on evalGuard and source-read matches; for (d), prove both directions by contradiction using constructor possibilities of OrB32Step and execOrB32 definitions.

theorem_obligations.intent: On true predicate and successful source reads, the destination is written with bitwise OR of source operands.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If evalGuard is true and both source reads return va, vb, then execOrB32 returns an executed post-state where the target destination register contains orValue va vb.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_execOrB32_guard_true_writes_or_result (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va) (hb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb) : ∃ s', execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (orValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va
hb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: ∃ s', execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (orValue va vb)
strength_risks: Requires explicit source-read and guard hypotheses; this avoids strengthening to a total-state claim unavailable in source and bounded semantics.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The conclusion constrains a concrete register value equation, directly instantiating the PTX text `d = a | b`.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Use hguard, ha, hb to expose executed branch of execOrB32, rewrite hd, and simplify the updateDestination expression at reg r.

theorem_obligations.intent: A relation step with destination bit-bucket leaves state unchanged.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any step OrB32Step s i s' with i.d = Destination.bitBucket, we have s' = s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_bitBucket_noop (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket) : s' = s
strength_risks: This uses design/architecture inference for `_` destination, not an explicit or.b32-only source claim in bounded semantics.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The bit-bucket constructor is present in the local Destination type; this checks its no-op behavior in the relational step and is therefore implementation-relevant.

theorem_obligations.intent: Executed steps modify only value registers and preserve predicate registers in the bounded model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: Assuming an executed step with resolved sources and true guard, all predicate-register lookups are equal between pre and post states.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32_OrB32Step_preserves_predicates_when_executed (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (va vb : B32) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hasa : readSource1 s i.a = some va) (hasb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb) : ∀ p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
hasa : readSource1 s i.a = some va
hasb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The bounded state includes predicates; asserting their pointwise frame property excludes hidden predicate writes and checks the scope restriction is respected.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: From executed constructor, reduce via h and hguard/hasa/hasb to definition of updateDestination, which updates only valueRegs and leaves predRegs unchanged.
